טָפֵל m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding)
1) attachment, of secondary import, opposed עיקר. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 39 ולוט ט׳ לו (Variant נטפל) and Lot was merely an attachment to Abraham. Berakhot 12ᵇ ויציאת … ט׳ לו and the exodus from Egypt will be considered of secondary import to it (the redemption from the powers). Ib. 13ᵃ ויעקב ט׳ the name Jacob will be secondary to Israel; and from

—2) pl. טְפֵלִים, טְפֵלִין dependants, children, minors. Kiddushin 34ᵇ (reference. to Devarim XXXI, 12) ט׳ חייבין minors are obliged to appear; see טַף. Bava Batra 117ᵃ; and from—Yerushalmi Sheviit VII, beginning 37ᵇ תְּפֵילִין, see אֲלוּנְטִית II.—V. טְפֵלָה.

עִיקָּר, עִקָּר m. (עָקַר)
1) root. Kilayim VII, 1 הע׳ השני the second root (that of the slip, see אַרְכּוּבָה); and from—plural עִיקָּרִים, עִיקָּרִין, עִקָּ׳. Ib. 2 ועִקָּרֵיהֶם נראין and the roots of the sets are visible. Shabbat XIV, 3 כוס ע׳ root-drink (a medicine for gonorrhœa). Tosefta Yevamot VIII, 4 האיש … כוס ע׳ שלא יוליד a man must not take a root-drink for the purpose of becoming impotent. Shabbat l. common gender. שמן ע׳ oil in which roots have been soaked. Yerushalmi Shekalim VI, beginning 49ᶜ שבו שולקין את הע׳ (oil) in which they boiled the roots (for frankincense); Horayot 11ᵇ; Kerith. 5ᵃ משלק בו הע׳. Ib.Kerith. 5ᵃ משלק בו הע׳. Ib. והלא לסוך הע׳ אינו סופק but there was not even oil enough to oint the roots (much less to soak them). Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Parah, p. 40ᵇ; Midrash Tanḥuma Chukat 8, and e. מביאין ע׳ ומעשנין וכ׳ they get certain roots (and kindle them), and let the smoke rise under him; and e.—Transferred origin. Ketubot 77ᵃ מעִיקָּרוֹ from its origin (shaft), see חָתַךְ.—עִיקַּר מיטרין, see מִיטְרִין.

—2) essence, reality, main object, chief. Yerushalmi Rosh Hashanah III, end, 59ᵃ עיקרו לא נחש הוא (not עיקרה) is not its (the saraf’s) real name naḥash? Sanhedrin 87ᵃ דבר שעיקרו מדברי וכ׳ a thing (law) which in its main aspect is found in the Torah, but the details of which are based on Soferic tradition (see סוֹפֵר). Yerushalmi Sotah VI, 21ᵃ top ע׳ עדותו the main testimony in the case. Berakhot 12ᵇ (reference. to Jeremiah XXIII, 7, sq.) לא שתעקר … אלא שתהא שעבוד מלכיות ע׳ וכ׳ not that the memory of the exodus from Egypt will be entirely effaced, but the delivery from servitude to the empires will be the chief event commemorated, and the exodus from Egypt subordinate to it (see טָפֵל). Ib. 13ᵃ ישראל ע׳ Israel will be the chief name. Ruth Rabbah to IV, 11, and e., see מְסוּבֶּה. Ib. (play on עקרה, Breishit XXIX, 31) ורחל היתה עיקרו … ורחל עֲקָרָה עִיקָּרָה Rachel was his (Jacob’s) main wife, for we read, ‘and Rachel was ʿḳʿăḳarah which means ʿiḳḳarah (the chief); Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 71 רחל היתה עיקרו של בית Rachel was the chief person of the household. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 14 (play on קערת, Bamidbar VII, 61) אל תקרי קערת אלא עִקֶּרֶת … עִקֶּרֶת הבית היא היתה עיקר ביתו וכ׳ read not ḳaʿărath, but ʿiḳḳereth, typical of Rachel who was the chief of the house: she was the chief person &c. Sukkah 50ᵇ ע׳ שירה בכלי the chief element in the Temple music is instrumental music; ע׳ שירה בפה the song is the essential element; and see from—טעם כע׳, see טַעַם.—כפר בע׳, see כָּפַר.—לא כל ע׳ not at all. Sanhedrin 22ᵃ לא נשתנה כל ע׳ has not at all been changed. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 16 אסור ליגע בה כל ע׳ must not touch her at all; and from—[In later Hebr. literature: עִיקָּרִים עִקָּ׳ principles of faith.]

עָקַר (Biblical Hebrew; compare עקב) [to be curved, bent; denominative עִיקָּר root,]
1) to uproot, tear loose, detach, remove; to eradicate, undo, abolish, abrogate. Horayot 14ᵃ עוֹקֵר הרים; Sanhedrin 24ᵃ עוקר הרי הרים, see הַר. Pirkei Avot III, 17 הרוח באה ועוֹקַרְתּוֹ וכ׳ a wind comes and uproots it and turns it &c. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Ekha, p. 123ᵃ כל מקום שנאמר ארון עוקר דיורין ומכניס וכ׳ wherever Adon (Master) is mentioned in the Bible, it means (the landlord) that displaces tenants and imports tenants; ib. עוקר כנענים וכ׳ who drives out the Canaanites and brings in the Israelites. Yerushalmi Yevamot I, 2ᵈ; ib. XIII, beginning 13ᵇ ממאנת … לַעֲקוֹר זיקת המת she may (on arriving at majority) refuse the Yabam, which has the effect of annulling her relation to her deceased husband. Ib. כל עמה מודיי שהיא עוֹקֶרֶת all agree that by doing so she annuls her marriage to her deceased husband. Pesachim 101ᵇ עָקְרוּ רגליהן לצאת when they detached their feet, in order to go. Shabbat 5ᵃ ע׳ ממקומו וכ׳ (subaudi רגליו) he moved from his place and received it. Yerushalmi Beitzah V, 63ᵃ bottom of page, see קִיפּוּץ. Megillah 5ᵇ בקש לעקור תשעה וכ׳ wanted to abolish the fast of the Ninth of Pirkei Avot Pesachim 115ᵇ אין עוֹקְרִין את השלחן we do not remove the table (see comment.); and see from—Part. pass. עָקוּר; f. עֲקוּרָה; plural עֲקוּרִים, עְקוּרִין; עֲקוּרוֹת a) uprooted, torn out. Peah VI, 9 תבואה ע׳ loose (cut) grain, שאינה ע׳ still in the ground.—b) = עָקָר [rootless,] barren, impotent. Yevamot 64ᵃ יצחק אבינו ע׳ היה Isaac was impotent; שניהם ע׳ היו both of them (Isaac and Rebecca) were impotent. Ib. מפני מה היו אבותינו ע׳ wherefore were our ancestors childless (until they prayed)?; and from—Bekhoroth 44ᵇ (reference. to Devarim VII, 14 ועקרה) שלא תהא תפלתך ע׳ וכ׳ that thy prayer shall not be fruitless before the Lord; Yalkut Devarim 884 שלא … ע׳ מלפני המקום that thy prayer shall not be removed from before the Lord; שלא יהא ביתך עקור מן התלמידים (not עקורה) that thy house shall not be deprived of scholars.

—2) to mutilate, hamstring; to make barren, see infra.

Nifal - נֱעֶקַר to be uprooted; to be removed, eradicated, destroyed. Yerushalmi Kilayim III, 28ᶜ bottom of page נֶעֶקְרוּ הראשונים if the first seeds have been taken out. Berakhot IX, 1 הרואה … מקום שנֶעֶקְרָה וכ׳ he who sees … a place from which an idol has been removed (by destruction). Ib. 12ᵇ לא שתֵּעָקֵר … ממקומה וכ׳ not that the memory of the going out from Egypt will be removed from its place (entirely extinct) &c., see עִיקָּר. Ib.ᵇ לא שיֵעָקֵר יעקב וכ׳ not that the name of Jacob will entirely fall into disuse; and from

Hifil - הֶעֱקִיר to make barren (עָקָר). Shir HaShirim Rabbah to II, 14 מפני מה הֶעֱקַרְתִּי אתכן why did I decree that you be childless? Because I desired to hear your prayer; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 45 עִקּרְתִּי Piël (or עָקַרְתִּי Kal).

Piël - עִיקֵּר
1) to uproot; to tear loose &c. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 42 מְעַקַּר בגפנים tried to uproot the vines (destroy the entire nation); Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 11. Ib. המן … לעַקֵּר וכ׳ Haman … undertook to destroy the vines; Breishit Rabbah l. common gender. ביקש לַעֲקוֹר הגפן כלה. Chullin V, 3 המעקר he who tears loose the organs to be cut at slaughtering (see סִימָן); and from

—2) to unfit, mutilate, hamstring; to make barren. Masechet Masechet Smachot Chaldaic VIII שורפין ומְעַקְּרִין לפני מלכים you may burn (clothes &c.) and hamstring horses at a king’s death; Pirkei Avot Zar. 11ᵃ עוֹקְרִין; Tosefta Shabbat VII (VIII), 19 עוקרין; see עִיקּוּר. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 45, see supra; and e.

Nithpaël - נִתְעַקֵּר to be made barren. Ib. למה נִתְעַקְּרוּ האמהות וכ׳ why were the Mothers allowed to be childless? Because the Lord desired to hear their prayers; Shir HaShirim Rabbah l. common gender.; and e.

שִׁעְבּוּד, שִׁי׳ m. (preceding)
1) subjection, servitude, oppression. Berakhot 12ᵇ שיהא ש׳ מלכיות וכ׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. שתהא) that the delivery from servitude to the empires &c., see עִיקָּר. Ib. 34ᵇ, and e. ש׳ מלכיות, see מַלְכוּת. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to II, 14 מפני מה … כדי שיצאו … בלא ש׳ why were the wives of the patriarchs barren (for a time)? In order that many (of the four-hundred) years (Breishit XV, 13) might pass without servitude; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 45. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 44 אף אני בש׳ shall I, too, be in slavery?; and from

—2) ש׳ קרקעות (or ש׳ only) pledge, hypothecary obligation, landed security. Bava Metzia 4ᵇ משום דהוה ליה שטר ש׳ ק׳ … כפירת ש׳ ק׳ because a note of indebtedness implies a hypothecary obligation (that the debtor’s landed property is pledged to the creditor), and no oath is assigned on a disputed hypothecary obligation; Shevuot 37ᵇ; Ketubot 87ᵇ. Bava Metzia 14ᵃ שבח שְׁפַר וש׳ וכ׳ the scribe must ask for authorization to insert, in a deed of sale of land, ‘amelioration’, ‘best land’ and ‘pledge’, i.e. that the seller pledges his land, and this the best portions of it, for indemnity to the buyer in case of seizure for the seller’s debt, this indemnity to include the improvements eventually made by the buyer; and from

sections.en: The Sages rejected this claim and they said to him that these verses do not mean that in the future the exodus from Egypt will be uprooted from its place and will be mentioned no more. Rather, redemption from the subjugation of the kingdoms will be primary and the exodus from Egypt will be secondary.
sections.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שֶׁתֵּעָקֵר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם מִמְּקוֹמָהּ, אֶלָּא שֶׁתְּהֵא שִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיוֹת עִיקָּר, וִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם טָפֵל לוֹ.

comments.en:
“Your name will no longer be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations” (Genesis 17:5).
“Your name will no longer be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham” – bar Kappara said: Anyone who calls Abraham Abram violates a prohibition. Rabbi Levi said: [He violates] a positive commandment, and a prohibition: “Your name will no longer be called Abram” – a prohibition; “but your name will be Abraham” – a positive commandment. But you see that the members of the Great Assembly called him Abram, as it is stated: “You are the Lord the God, who chose Abram, and took him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and set his name as Abraham.” (Nehemiah 9:7) That case is different, as [it means:] You chose him while he was still called Abram.
Similarly, does one who calls Sarah Sarai violate a positive commandment? It was [only] he [Abraham] who was commanded regarding her.
Similarly, does one who calls Israel Jacob violate a positive commandment? It is taught: [God’s intent was] not that the name Jacob should be uprooted from its place, but rather, “[Your name is Jacob]…rather, Israel shall be your name” (Genesis 35:10) – Israel is to be the primary name, and Jacob the secondary name. Rabbi Zavda in the name of Rabbi Aḥa: In any case, “your name is Jacob…rather, Israel” – Jacob is the primary name, and Israel is in addition to it.
comments.he: וְלֹא יִקָּרֵא עוֹד אֶת שִׁמְךָ אַבְרָם וְהָיָה שִׁמְךָ אַבְרָהָם (בראשית יז, ה), בַּר קַפָּרָא אָמַר כָּל מִי שֶׁהוּא קוֹרֵא לְאַבְרָהָם אַבְרָם עוֹבֵר בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה. רַבִּי לֵוִי אָמַר בַּעֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, וְלֹא יִקָּרֵא עוֹד שִׁמְךָ אַבְרָם, בְּלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, וְהָיָה שִׁמְךָ אַבְרָהָם, בַּעֲשֵׂה. וַהֲרֵי אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה קָרְאוּ אוֹתוֹ אַבְרָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (נחמיה ט, ז): אַתָּה הוּא ה' הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר בָּחַרְתָּ בְּאַבְרָם וְהוֹצֵאתוֹ מֵאוּר כַּשְׂדִּים וְשַׂמְתָּ שְׁמוֹ אַבְרָהָם, דִּלְּמָא שַׁנְיָה הִיא שֶׁעַד שֶׁהוּא אַבְרָם בָּחַרְתָּ בּוֹ, דִּכְוָתָהּ הַקּוֹרֵא לְשָׂרָה שָׂרַי עוֹבֵר בַּעֲשֵׂה, אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּצְטַוָּוה עָלֶיהָ. דִּכְוָתָהּ הַקּוֹרֵא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל יַעֲקֹב עוֹבֵר בַּעֲשֵׂה, תָּנֵי לֹא שֶׁיֵּעָקֵר שֵׁם יַעֲקֹב מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, אֶלָּא (בראשית לה, י): כִּי אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל יִהְיֶה שְׁמֶךָ, יִשְׂרָאֵל עִקָּר וְיַעֲקֹב טְפֵלָה. רַבִּי זַבְדָא בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי אַחָא מִכָּל מָקוֹם שִׁמְךָ יַעֲקֹב כִּי אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל, יַעֲקֹב עִקָּר וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹסִיף עָלָיו.
וכיוצא בו אתה אומר: משמעות הביטוי "לא יאמר" או "לא יזכירו" אינה החלטית, ודבר זה נלמד מן הכתוב "לא יקרא שמך עוד יעקב כי אם ישראל יהיה שמך" (בראשית לה, י), שאף שם הפירוש הוא

God said to him,
